stem: A child in cardiac arrest has intraosseous access after failed IV attempts, and the team wants blood tests before giving medications; which approach is best?

options.text: Take blood from the IO needle before any medications are given
Take blood from IV access only if it is quick and does not delay medications
Always delay adrenaline until a full blood panel is obtained
Take blood from IO access because it is faster than IV
Do not take any blood samples during resuscitation

explanation: Take blood from IV access only if it is quick and does not delay medications. This matches the guidance that blood collection should not delay time-critical treatment, and IV is preferred over IO for sampling in this context.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Paediatric Basic Life Support / Circulation

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the guidance prefers IV sampling, not IO, and blood collection must not delay medications.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because blood may be taken from IV access only when it is quick and does not delay medications.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because adrenaline should not be delayed for a full blood panel in cardiac arrest.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the guidance does not recommend taking blood from IO access for this purpose.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because blood samples can be taken if it is quick and does not delay emergency treatment.
